<reason>B won on coverage, metric, and Latin America. PRO proved zero deaths inside but never bridged to city-wide fewer deaths; CON's fraction-of-injections, poisoned-supply-everywhere, and Vancouver-province test stuck, and PRO's refusal of a city-wide test as a magic number looked evasive. On Latin America PRO conceded deaths-averted is smaller and shifted to disorder, while CON kept naloxone-irrelevant-for-smoked-base and fixed-queue-for-armed-groups live. Factory-trust reframe could not beat window-vs-supervision cost point.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B Rebuttal 2 A1-A2: seatbelt bolted to one chair vs naloxone in pocket that rides everywhere, plus mobile doorway vs permanent published facility, which turned PRO's reversal count and no-loitering rules into a coverage failure and exposed the LatAm concession.</best_rebuttal>
